Luna Optimizer

See what makes a Luna playable heavy and shrink it in a few clicks, without a full Luna build. It works inside Unity or in a web browser while Unity is open.

1Service image

2Problem

Playable ads have hard size caps per ad network (for example 5 MB). Finding what to cut is slow:

  • The only way to know the real size is a full Luna build, which takes minutes, and its report is hard to act on.
  • Texture and sound settings live in Luna's own window, one asset at a time, with no preview of the result.
  • It is unclear which change saves the most, and what breaks if an asset is removed.
  • Each try-build-check loop costs minutes, so teams stop optimizing early or ship over the cap.

3Solution

Luna Optimizer runs Luna's own pipeline locally and shows the result immediately.

Measure without building

Quick predict runs Luna's size statistics on the project: total against the network cap and what ships per asset type.

One-click optimizations

Pick the smallest texture format at a chosen quality, trim silence from sounds, make sounds mono. Every change is previewed with its exact saving before it is saved.

Safe changes

Nothing is written until "Save to Luna", saves go through Luna's own settings, and every save can be undone.

In Unity or in the browser

Simple and Manual modes inside Unity, or every feature in a browser tab (Supercent → Luna Optimizer (Browser)) while Unity runs it: Overview, Textures, Sounds, Models & Other, Exclusions, scene switch and Undo.

4Expected impact

~0.2 sscene estimate without a build: 1,703 KB vs 1,711 KB actual
0 Bdifference from Luna's real output for textures
772,255 Bscripts, the same number Luna's build reports
53,000 BOpus sound, the same size as the built file
  • Optimizing and navigating is much faster: decisions are made from a ranked list, not from trial builds.
  • Designers and artists can see the effect of a format, size or trim change before anyone builds.
  • Fewer "over the cap" surprises at the end of a project. Already used on ThemeparkManager and SmashDown.

5Limitations & resources

Limitations

  • Unity must be open: the browser page is a remote control for the editor, on this computer only.
  • The total estimate is larger than the final build (the real build is smaller); a final Luna build is still needed before delivery.
  • Verified with Luna 7.2.0 on macOS; other versions need a check.
  • Opus audio is smaller but needs recent iOS; devices not yet tested.

Resources for a real rollout

  • Shared package linked into each project (one copy, updates reach every project).
  • A Luna install with Node and ffmpeg (already part of Luna).
  • Time to check the estimate gap on more projects and test on Windows.
  • Optional: a hosted, read-only size report so PMs can see results without Unity.
